note: Plain explanations of the course-written patterns, ko-par-g001 to ko-par-g062 (pattern id -> one line for a beginner: what the learner can say with it, about 60 characters at most, lower case, no full stop). Applied by scripts/generate-pack-ko.mjs as each pattern's ds; the TOPIK patterns keep the english line of their source, and --check fails for a course-written pattern without an entry. Each was written after reading the sentences of the pack that use the pattern.

explanations.ko-par-g001: asks a yes/no question: say a statement with rising tone
explanations.ko-par-g002: leave out who you mean when it is clear
explanations.ko-par-g003: a noun before a noun describes it: Chinese + teacher
explanations.ko-par-g004: asks 'what about …?' after something was said
explanations.ko-par-g045: let's do it: 우리 and the polite verb
explanations.ko-par-g005: says everyone in the group does it or is it
explanations.ko-par-g047: yes; answers a question or agrees
explanations.ko-par-g007: a little; goes before an adjective
explanations.ko-par-g028: adds 들: more than one person or thing
explanations.ko-par-g008: says when it happens: the time goes first or before the verb
explanations.ko-par-g009: for a length of time: 동안 after the duration
explanations.ko-par-g010: a little of something; 조금 goes after the noun
explanations.ko-par-g024: this or that; goes before a noun
explanations.ko-par-g013: says a year: a number and 년
explanations.ko-par-g046: reads a year such as 2026 in Sino-Korean numbers
explanations.ko-par-g014: a number plus 번: a numbered item, such as a room
explanations.ko-par-g044: half a unit: 반 before the counter
explanations.ko-par-g017: eleven to nineteen: 열 and a native number
explanations.ko-par-g018: asks how much someone does something
explanations.ko-par-g020: asks with 뭐, 누구 or 어디 in the place of the answer
explanations.ko-par-g019: says something is in front of, behind or beside
explanations.ko-par-g021: says what you call someone or something
explanations.ko-par-g022: some; a few of a group
explanations.ko-par-g023: this or that over there; goes before a noun
explanations.ko-par-g025: says what someone says, quoting the words
explanations.ko-par-g026: too, or so; goes before an adjective
explanations.ko-par-g029: says what you think: it is …
explanations.ko-par-g030: polite past: did not do it
explanations.ko-par-g032: hundreds and thousands: the number before 백 or 천
explanations.ko-par-g049: two before ten, hundred or thousand: 이십, 이백, 이천
explanations.ko-par-g033: asks how big, or how old someone is
explanations.ko-par-g034: polite title after a name: Mr. or Ms.
explanations.ko-par-g054: marks the place something is, or happens
explanations.ko-par-g037: asks how it is done: 어떻게 before the verb
explanations.ko-par-g042: month names: a Sino-Korean number and 월
explanations.ko-par-g058: months and days of a date use Sino-Korean numbers
explanations.ko-par-g062: I will do it: a promise or decision
explanations.ko-par-g040: first, second, third: 번째 after a number
explanations.ko-par-g041: which one; goes before a noun
explanations.ko-par-g043: big and small place values together; zeros are left out
